flags: PARTIAL DRAFT: the ADOT corridor plan cited by current and material is absent. Cache 00 has no byway table entries. The specific designation, date, official extent and designating body’s scenic rationale cannot be verified; not asserted in public copy.
Driving evidence is limited to US 191’s route and Round Rock’s highway visibility. No supported trip duration, road-surface description, grades or curves; overview and moments are deliberately short.

Dropped unsupported current claims: wash crossings; roadside hogans, shade houses, corrals and grazing livestock; Many Farms Lake capacity of 25,000 acre-feet; Round Rock trading post’s 1887 date, location and regional primacy; lake bird counts and swans; Rock Point’s former “standing metal” name and windmill derivation.

No Navajo Nation or community-authored source is cached for names or traditions. Tsé Nikání is translated as “round flat-topped rock” in cache 05; current’s “flat mesa rock” wording is not independently supported. Conflicting mesa-climbing legends in cache 05 omitted.

Moment coordinates are preserved from current and identify the communities, not a mesa viewpoint or authorized access. Northbound order is supported by cache 08; material strip miles run southward and omit Round Rock.
Current slickrock-ridge motifs retained as sandstone-landform context; no ridge or slickrock walking access is asserted.
